pages.text: Farming in Tilth follows real agronomy. Every block of ground has a $(thing)soil texture$() (sand, silt, clay and their mixtures) that sets how much water it holds, how fast it drains and how well it keeps nutrients.
Crops grow on $(thing)thermal time$(): warmth, not ticks. A cold spring slows them, a frost can kill them, and each crop has its own season.

Tilled soil remembers its $(thing)nutrients$(), $(thing)pH$(), $(thing)organic matter$(), moisture and compaction, and every crop draws on them. Rain fills hollows into $(thing)ponds$(), and water can optionally be made finite in the config.
Your own body needs a varied $(thing)diet$(), and well-grown food is more nourishing.

Nothing here is meant to be a grind: every rate is in the config, and the commands under $(thing)/tilth$() let you inspect everything. If something surprises you, look at it with the Soil Probe or $(thing)/tilth crop$(): the reason is always shown.
